To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hardware impairments have to be taken into consideration in the design of bidirectional FD MIMO systems and that a design that takes into account the hardware distortions can significantly improve the system performance.

(i) the hardware impairments aware design is essential for systems with a high level of hardware impairments, and (ii) the proposed distortion-aware design is more efficient than the distortion-unaware design for systems with a low thermal variance.
the hardware distortions have a considerable impact on bidirectional FD MIMO-OFDM systems and should be taken into account during the design process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a hardware impairment-aware transceiver design for bidirectional full-duplex MIMO-OFDM communication systems.

the design of a distortion-aware transceiver for a bidirectional full-duplex MIMO system, where the effects of hardware distortions and channel state information errors are taken into account in the design process.

the design and optimization of bidirectional FD MIMO OFDM systems, taking into account the effects of hardware distortions, and it can be used as a guideline for the design of practical FD MIMO OFDMA systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a distortion-aware design should be applied for all systems.
the distortion-aware design outperforms the distortion-unaware design in all cases, and the distortion-aware design with imperfect CSI performs better than that with perfect CSI, in most cases.
the proposed design outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of sum rate and bit-error rate, and that it is more robust against channel estimation errors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed designs can provide an efficient way to mitigate the hardware distortions in bidirectional FD MIMO systems.
the hardware distortion aware design can be a promising approach to mitigate the hardware distortion effect in FD MIMO systems.

, for a system with high thermal noise variance, it is not necessary to apply the distortion-aware design, whereas, for a system that is subject to a high hardware distortion and low thermal noise variance, the proposed designs should be applied to achieve a satisfactory performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a distortion-aware design can be implemented at low computational costs, with the benefit of achieving substantial performance improvements.
the proposed design is capable of mitigating the impact of hardware distortions on the system performance, even when the channel state information is erroneous.
the distortion-aware design outperforms the distortion-unaware design in terms of sum rate, especially when the hardware distortion is high, or when the thermal noise variance is low.
